FIVE COMMON MOVEMENTS

A thoughtful place to start.

Hand and wrist movements drawn from NHS and hand-therapy guidance.
Choose those appropriate for your condition with your therapist.

How the camera estimates movement

Finger curls use the average 3D PIP flexion angle of four fingers. Thumb opposition uses thumb–little fingertip distance divided by palm length; this is a movement proxy, not thumb joint ROM. Finger spread uses the angle between index and little-finger proximal bones.

Wrist tracking automatically finds an exposed section of forearm in the camera image, using the detected hand to sample appearance and find the forearm’s edges. It fits a line to the visible forearm and measures the hand angle against that line. No elbow, upper body or manual reference is required. Use a plain contrasting background and show several inches of uncovered forearm. If the outline is unclear or unstable, measurement pauses.

The signed angle estimates motion in the camera plane, with aspect-ratio correction. Use a side view for wrist bend and a view perpendicular to side-to-side movement for wrist deviation. These two exercises use the same projected angle in different viewing planes; the camera cannot reliably distinguish those planes automatically. Forearm drift is checked, but depth, occlusion, skin-colored backgrounds and camera movement can still create error. Recalibrate if you change position. This experimental appearance-based detector has not been validated on patient recordings.

Calibration captures two stable, comfortable positions for each exercise. Games use a fraction of that span, with dwell times and tracking-loss pauses. No prescribed clinical range or repetitions are assumed. Single-camera estimates are not clinically validated and do not replace a goniometer or assessment.

Camera processing happens locally in a classic worker using MediaPipe Hand and an automatic forearm-outline detector. No video or landmark stream is recorded or uploaded. Session summaries stay in this browser. The host receives ordinary site requests.
